events.title: Georges-André Chevallaz takes power
events.summary: Georges-André Chevallaz was a Swiss historian, politician and member of the Swiss Federal Council (1974–1983).

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Tunisia vs Résistance Armée Tunisienne
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Tunisia and Résistance Armée Tunisienne over control of the government, starting 1980-01-28. This episode was active in 1 year (1980–1980), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1980-01-28.

events.title: Gunnar Thoroddsen takes power
events.summary: Gunnar Thoroddsen was the prime minister of Iceland from 1980 to 1983.

events.title: 1980 Canadian federal election
events.summary: The 1980 Canadian federal election was held on February 18, 1980, to elect members of the House of Commons of Canada of the 32nd Parliament of Canada. It was called when the budget of the minority Progressive Conservative government led by Prime Minister Joe Clark was defeated in the Commons.

events.title: 1980 Saint Kitts and Nevis general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Saint Kitts and Nevis on 18 February 1980. Although the Saint Kitts and Nevis Labour Party won a plurality of the elected seats, the People's Action Movement (PAM) were able to form a coalition government with the Nevis Reformation Party which held a one-seat majority. PAM leader Kennedy Simmonds became Premier.

events.title: Coup: 1980 Surinamese coup d'état
events.summary: The 1980 Surinamese coup d'état, usually referred to as the Sergeants' Coup, was a military coup in Suriname which occurred on 25 February 1980, when a group of 16 sergeants of the Surinamese Armed Forces (SKM) led by Dési Bouterse overthrew the government of Prime Minister Henck Arron with a violent coup d'état.

events.title: 1980 Andalusian autonomy initiative referendum
events.summary: A referendum on the initiative of the Andalusian autonomy process was held in Andalusia on Thursday, 28 February 1980. Voters were asked whether they ratified a proposed initiative for the provinces of Almería, Cádiz, Córdoba, Granada, Huelva, Jaén, Málaga and Seville to organize themselves into an autonomous community of Spain throughout the legal…

events.title: Pierre Trudeau takes power
events.summary: Joseph Philippe Pierre Yves Elliott Trudeau was a Canadian politician, lawyer, jurist, academic, author, and journalist who served as the 15th prime minister of Canada from 1968 to 1979 and from 1980 to 1984. He served as the leader of the Opposition from 1979 to 1980.

events.title: 1980 Romanian parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Romania on 9 March 1980. The Front of Socialist Unity and Democracy (FDUS), dominated by the Romanian Communist Party (PCR) and including other mass organisations, was the only organisation that contested the election. No prospective candidate could run for office without the Front's prior approval.

events.title: Berber Spring
events.summary: The Berber Spring was a period of political protest and civil activism in 1980, claiming recognition of the Amazigh identity and language in Algeria, with events mainly taking place in Kabylia and Algiers.

events.title: 1980 Polish parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Poland on 23 March 1980. The results, like with the other elections in communist Poland, were controlled by the communist government. The results of the 1980 election exactly duplicated the 1976 elections, which were only marginally different from those of the preceding years.

events.title: 1980 Swedish nuclear power referendum
events.summary: A non-binding referendum on nuclear power was held in Sweden on 23 March 1980. Three proposals were put to voters. The second option, the gradual phasing out of nuclear power, won a narrow plurality of the vote, receiving 39.1% of the ballots cast to 38.7% for option 3. Option 1 was the least popular, receiving only 18.9% of the votes.

events.title: Treaty signed: United Nations Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods
events.summary: The United Nations Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods (CISG), sometimes known as the Vienna Convention, is a multilateral treaty that establishes a uniform framework for international commerce. As of September 2023, it has been ratified or acceded to by 97 countries, representing two-thirds of world trade.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Liberia vs Military faction (forces of Samuel Doe)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Liberia and Military faction (forces of Samuel Doe) over control of the government, starting 1980-04-12. This episode was active in 1 year (1980–1980), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1980-04-14.

events.title: European Council meeting
events.summary: EU heads of state or government meet as the European Council. Council presidency: Italy.

events.title: 1980 Honduran Constituent Assembly election
events.summary: Constituent Assembly elections were held in Honduras on 20 April 1980. In July the Assembly elected Policarpo Paz García as president.

events.title: 1980 Antiguan general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Antigua and Barbuda on 24 April 1980. They were won by the governing Antigua Labour Party. ALP leader Vere Bird was re-elected as Prime Minister of Antigua and Barbuda. Voter turnout was 77.1%.

events.title: Inauguration of Beatrix
events.summary: The inauguration of Beatrix as Queen of the Netherlands took place on 30 April 1980 at the Nieuwe Kerk in Amsterdam. Beatrix ascended the throne immediately following the abdication of her mother Juliana earlier that day.

events.title: 1980 Nepalese governmental system referendum
events.summary: A referendum on the system of government was held in Nepal on 2 May 1980. Voters were offered the choice between a non-partisan panchayat system and a multi-party system. The panchayat system received a slim majority of 54.99%, whereas Multi-Party System only received 45.2% of the total votes. Voter turnout was 66.9%.

events.title: Lazar Koliševski takes power
events.summary: Lazar Koliševski was a Macedonian Yugoslav communist political leader in the Socialist Republic of Macedonia and briefly in the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. He was closely allied with Josip Broz Tito.

events.title: 1980 Greek presidential election
events.summary: An indirect election for the position of President of the Hellenic Republic was held by the Hellenic Parliament in April–May 1980.

events.title: George Rallis takes power
events.summary: Georgios Ioannou Rallis, anglicised to George Rallis, was a Greek conservative politician and Prime Minister of Greece from 1980 to 1981.

events.title: Cvijetin Mijatović takes power
events.summary: Cvijetin "Majo" Mijatović was a Yugoslav communist politician who served as President of the Presidency of Yugoslavia from 1980 to 1981. He also served as President of the League of Communists of Bosnia and Herzegovina from 1965 to 1969.

events.title: Coup d'état of May Seventeenth
events.summary: The Coup d'état of May Seventeenth was a military coup d'état staged by General Chun Doo-hwan on 17 May 1980 against the civilian government of President Choi Kyu-hah in South Korea.

events.title: 1980 Austrian presidential election
events.summary: Presidential elections were held in Austria on 18 May 1980. Supported by both major parties, the ruling Socialist Party and opposition Austrian People's Party, incumbent president Rudolf Kirchschläger was re-elected with a landslide of 80% of the vote.

events.title: 1980 Quebec referendum
events.summary: The 1980 Quebec independence referendum was the first referendum in Quebec on the place of Quebec within Canada and whether Quebec should pursue a path toward sovereignty. The referendum was called by Quebec's Parti Québécois (PQ) government, which advocated secession from Canada.

events.title: 1980 Czechoslovak presidential election
events.summary: The 1980 Czechoslovak presidential election was carried out on 22 May 1980 by the deputies of the two houses of the nation's parliament, the Federal Assembly, rather than by popular vote. Gustáv Husák was re-elected for his second term.

events.title: 1980 vote of no confidence in the government of Adolfo Suárez
events.summary: A motion of no confidence in the Spanish government of Adolfo Suárez was debated and voted in the Congress of Deputies between 28 and 30 May 1980. It was brought by Spanish Socialist Workers' Party (PSOE) leader Felipe González.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Ethiopia – Somalia (Ogaden)
events.summary: UCDP records an interstate conflict between Government of Ethiopia (backed by Government of Cuba) and Government of Somalia over control of Ogaden, starting 1980-05-31. This episode was active in 1 year (1980–1980), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1980-12-03.

events.title: 1980 Hungarian parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Hungary on 8 June 1980. The Hungarian Socialist Workers' Party was the only party to contest the elections, and won 252 of the 352 seats, with the remaining 100 going to independents selected by the party.

events.title: European Council meeting
events.summary: EU heads of state or government meet as the European Council. Council presidency: Italy.

events.title: Masayoshi Ito takes power
events.summary: Masayoshi Ito was a Japanese political figure. He served as acting Prime Minister of Japan in 1980 after the sudden death of Masayoshi Ōhira. He then served as foreign minister of Japan from 1980 to 1981.

events.title: Diamond v. Chakrabarty
events.summary: Diamond v. Chakrabarty, 447 U.S. 303 (1980), was a United States Supreme Court case dealing with whether living organisms can be patented. Writing for a five-justice majority, Chief Justice Warren E.

events.title: 6th G7 summit
events.summary: The 6th G7 Summit was held at Venice, Italy, between 22 and 23 June 1980. The venue for the summit meetings was the island of San Giorgio Maggiore in the Venetian lagoon.

events.title: 1980 Icelandic presidential election
events.summary: Presidential elections were held in Iceland on 29 June 1980. The result was a victory for Vigdís Finnbogadóttir, who received 34% of the vote. She became the world's first democratically elected female president.

events.title: Coup: Nojeh coup plot
events.summary: The "Saving Iran's Great Uprising" more commonly known as the Nojeh coup d'état, was a plan to overthrow the newly established Islamic Republic of Iran and its government of Abolhassan Banisadr and Ruhollah Khomeini.

events.title: Zenko Suzuki takes power
events.summary: Zenkō Suzuki was a Japanese politician who served as prime minister of Japan from 1980 to 1982.

events.title: 1980 Republican Party presidential primaries
events.summary: From January 21 to June 28, 1980, voters of the Republican Party chose its nominee for president in the 1980 United States presidential election.

events.title: 1980 Dominican general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Dominica on 21 July 1980. The result was a victory for the Dominica Freedom Party, which won 17 of the 21 seats, whilst the ruling Dominica Labour Party lost all 16 seats after nineteen years in power. Voter turnout was 80.2%.

events.title: 1980 Honduran presidential election
events.summary: Constituent Assembly elections were held in Honduras on 20 April 1980. In July the Assembly elected Policarpo Paz García as president.

events.title: Terrorist attack: Bologna massacre
events.summary: The Bologna massacre was a terrorist bombing of the Bologna Centrale railway station in Bologna, Italy, on the morning of 2 August 1980, which killed 85 people and wounded over 200. Several members of the neo-fascist terrorist organization Nuclei Armati Rivoluzionari were sentenced for the bombing, although the group denied involvement.

events.title: 1980 Democratic Party presidential primaries
events.summary: From January 21 to June 3, 1980, voters of the Democratic Party chose its nominee for president in the 1980 United States presidential election.

events.title: 1980 Democratic National Convention
events.summary: The 1980 Democratic National Convention nominated President Jimmy Carter and Vice President Walter Mondale for reelection. The convention was held in Madison Square Garden in New York City from August 11 to August 14, 1980.

events.title: Stanisław Kania takes power
events.summary: Stanisław Kania was a Polish communist politician who served as the de facto leader of the Polish People's Republic as First Secretary of the ruling Polish United Workers' Party (PZPR) between September 1980 and October 1981.

events.title: 1980 Liechtenstein referendum
events.summary: A double referendum was held in Liechtenstein on 7 September 1980. Voters were asked whether they approved of the construction of a House of Arts and a national conference centre. The House of Arts was approved by 50.4% of voters, whilst the conference centre was rejected by 52.9% of voters.

events.title: Deng Xiaoping takes power
events.summary: Deng Xiaoping was a Chinese statesman, revolutionary, and political theorist who served as the paramount leader of the People's Republic of China (PRC) from 1978 to 1989.

events.title: 1980 Chilean constitutional referendum
events.summary: A constitutional referendum was held in Chile on 11 September 1980. The proposed new constitution would replace the 1925 constitution, and was approved by over two-thirds of voters.

events.title: 1980 Turkish presidential election
events.summary: The 1980 Turkish presidential election refers to the unsuccessful election process to choose the country's seventh president, to succeed Fahri Korutürk. The first round of the election was held on 12 March 1980. There were 115 unsuccessful rounds until 12 September 1980. The election ended with a coup d'état on that date.

events.title: Coup: 1980 Turkish coup d'état
events.summary: The 1980 Turkish coup d'état, headed by Chief of the General Staff General Kenan Evren, was the third coup d'état in the history of the Republic of Turkey, the previous having been the 1960 coup and the 1971 coup by memorandum.

events.title: Kenan Evren takes power (irregular seizure of power)
events.summary: Ahmet Kenan Evren was a Turkish military officer who served as the 7th president of Turkey from 1982 to 1989. He assumed the post by leading the 1980 military coup.

events.title: Battle of Khorramshahr (1980)
events.summary: The First Battle of Khorramshahr was a major battle in the Iran–Iraq War, beginning shortly after the Iraqi invasion of Iran in September 1980. Amidst the gruelling urban warfare in and around the city, Khorramshahr came to be referred to by the Iranians as Khuninshahr, as both sides had suffered heavy casualties in combat.

events.title: Iraq invades Iran, starting the Iran–Iraq War
events.summary: The Iran–Iraq War, also called the First Imposed War, Eight-Year War, or Sacred Defense by Iran, began with the Iraqi invasion of Iran in September 1980. After eight years of conflict, both countries accepted a ceasefire deal brokered by the United Nations, which became effective in August 1988.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Iran – Iraq (Various)
events.summary: UCDP records an interstate conflict between Government of Iran and Government of Iraq over territory and government, starting 1980-09-23. This episode was active in 9 years (1980–1988), 9 of them at war level (1,000+ battle deaths a year), and ended 1988-08-20.

events.title: 1980 Panamanian parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Panama on 28 September 1980, electing a new National Legislative Council.

events.title: 1980 Portuguese legislative election
events.summary: The 1980 Portuguese legislative election took place on 5 October. The election renewed all 250 members of the Assembly of the Republic.

events.title: 1980 West German federal election
events.summary: A federal election was held in West Germany on 5 October 1980 to elect the members of the 9th Bundestag. Although the CDU/CSU remained the largest faction in parliament, Helmut Schmidt of the Social Democratic Party remained Chancellor.

events.title: 6th Congress of the Workers' Party of Korea
events.summary: The 6th Congress of the Workers' Party of Korea (WPK) was held in the February 8 House of Culture in Pyongyang, North Korea, from 10 to 14 October 1980. The congress is the highest organ of the party, and is stipulated to be held every four years.

events.title: Treaty signed: Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons
events.summary: The United Nations Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons, concluded at Geneva on October 10, 1980, and entered into force in December 1983, seeks to prohibit or restrict the use of certain conventional weapons which are considered excessively injurious or whose effects are indiscriminate.

events.title: Arnaldo Forlani takes power
events.summary: Arnaldo Forlani was an Italian politician who served as Prime Minister of Italy from 1980 to 1981. He also held the office of Deputy Prime Minister of Italy, Minister of Foreign Affairs, and Minister of Defence.

events.title: 1980 South Korean constitutional referendum
events.summary: A constitutional referendum was held in South Korea on 22 October 1980. The changes to the constitution were approved by 91.6% of voters, with a turnout of 95.5%.

events.title: Treaty signed: Hague Convention on the Civil Aspects of International Child Abduction
events.summary: The Hague Convention on the Civil Aspects of International Child Abduction or Hague Abduction Convention is a multilateral treaty that provides an expeditious method to return a child who was wrongfully taken by a parent from one country to another country. In order for the Convention to apply, both countries must be Contracting States; i.e.

events.title: 1980 Jamaican general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Jamaica on 30 October 1980. The balance of power in the 60-seat Jamaican House of Representatives was dramatically-shifted. Prior to the vote, the People's National Party (PNP), led by Prime Minister Michael Manley, had a 47–13 majority over the Jamaica Labour Party (JLP), led by Edward Seaga.

events.title: Edward Seaga takes power
events.summary: Edward Philip George Seaga was a Jamaican politician and record producer. He was the fifth Prime Minister of Jamaica, from 1980 to 1989, and the leader of the Jamaica Labour Party from 1974 to 2005. He served as Leader of the Opposition from 1974 to 1980, and again from 1989 until January 2005.

events.title: 1980 United States presidential election
events.summary: Presidential elections were held in the United States on November 4, 1980. The Republican ticket of former California governor Ronald Reagan and former director of central intelligence George H. W. Bush defeated the Democratic ticket of incumbent president Jimmy Carter and vice president Walter Mondale, and the Independent ticket of Congressman John B.

events.title: Battle: Siege of Abadan
events.summary: The siege of Abadan was the encirclement of the city by Iraqi forces beginning in November 1980. The city had already been under almost daily bombardment since the early days of the war, which began the previous September.

events.title: Coup: 1980 Guinea-Bissau coup d'état
events.summary: The 1980 Guinea-Bissau coup d'état was a bloodless military coup that took place in Guinea-Bissau on 14 November 1980, led by Prime Minister General João Bernardo Vieira. It led to the deposition of President Luís Cabral, who held the office since 1973, while the country's War of Independence was still ongoing.

events.title: Earthquake: 1980 Irpinia earthquake
events.summary: The 1980 Irpinia earthquake took place in Italy on 23 November 1980, with a moment magnitude of 6.9 and a maximum Mercalli intensity of X (Extreme). It left at least 2,483 people dead, at least 7,700 injured, and 250,000 homeless.

events.title: Battle: Operation Morvarid
events.summary: Operation Morvarid was an operation launched by the Iranian Navy and Air Force against the Iraqi Navy sites on 27 November 1980 in response to Iraq positioning radar and monitoring equipment on the Mina Al-Bakr and Khor-al-Amaya oil rigs to counter Iranian air operations.

events.title: 1980 Uruguayan constitutional referendum
events.summary: A constitutional referendum was held in Uruguay on 30 November 1980 to decide whether to approve the new constitution drafted by the military dictatorship that had ruled Uruguay since 1973.

events.title: European Council meeting
events.summary: EU heads of state or government meet as the European Council. Council presidency: Luxembourg.

events.title: 1980 Portuguese presidential election
events.summary: A presidential election was held in Portugal on 7 December 1980, as according to the decree that approved the Constitution, which stipulated that the first term of the President would end three months after the end of the first legislature, on 14 October 1980.

events.title: José Napoleón Duarte takes power (irregular seizure of power)
events.summary: José Napoleón Duarte Fuentes was a Salvadoran politician who served as the 36th President of El Salvador from 1984 to 1989 during the Salvadoran Civil War. He was mayor of San Salvador before running for president in 1972. He lost, but the election is widely viewed as fraudulent.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Ethiopia vs OLF (Oromiya)
events.summary: UCDP records an internationalised civil conflict between Government of Ethiopia (backed by Government of Cuba) and OLF over control of Oromiya, starting 1980-12-31. This episode was active in 2 years (1980–1981), 1 of them at war level (1,000+ battle deaths a year), and ended 1981-12-31.

events.title: Kurt Furgler takes power
events.summary: Kurt Furgler was a Swiss politician and member of the Swiss Federal Council (1972–1986).

events.title: Battle: Operation Nasr
events.summary: Operation Nasr, also known as Operation Hoveyzeh, was a major battle in the Iran–Iraq War fought in early January 1981. It was the biggest tank battle of the war.

events.title: Ronald Reagan takes power
events.summary: Ronald Wilson Reagan was an American politician and actor who served as the 40th president of the United States from 1981 to 1989. A member of the Republican Party, he became an important figure in the American conservative movement. The period encompassing his presidency is known as the Reagan era.

events.title: First inauguration of Ronald Reagan
events.summary: The first inauguration of Ronald Reagan as the 40th president of the United States was held on Tuesday, January 20, 1981, at the West Front of the United States Capitol in Washington, D.C. This was the first inauguration to be held on the building's west side. This was the 49th inauguration and marked the commencement of Ronald Reagan's and George H. W.

events.title: Gro Harlem Brundtland takes power
events.summary: Gro Brundtland, known as Gro Harlem Brundtland, is a Norwegian stateswoman and former physician, who thrice served as the Prime Minister of Norway, and as the leader of the Labour Party from 1981 to 1992, and as the director-general of the World Health Organization from 1998 to 2003.

events.title: 26th Congress of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union
events.summary: The 26th Congress of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union opened on February 23, 1981, with a five-hour address by the General Secretary of the Communist Party and the chairman (president) of the Presidium of the Supreme Soviet Leonid Brezhnev. This was the last Congress for Brezhnev, who died in 1982.

events.title: Coup: 1981 Spanish coup attempt
events.summary: A coup d'état was attempted in Spain in February 1981 by right-wing, Francoist elements of the Civil Guard and the Spanish military. The failure of the coup marked the last serious attempt to revert Spain to a Francoist state and served to consolidate Spain's democratization process.

events.title: Leopoldo Calvo-Sotelo takes power
events.summary: Leopoldo Ramón Pedro Calvo-Sotelo y Bustelo, 1st Marquess of Ría de Ribadeo, was a Spanish civil engineer and politician who was Prime Minister of Spain from 1981 to 1982.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Ethiopia vs SLM (Sidamaland)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Ethiopia and SLM over control of Sidamaland, starting 1981-03-21. This episode was active in 1 year (1981–1981), 1 of them at war level (1,000+ battle deaths a year), and ended 1981-03-21.

events.title: European Council meeting
events.summary: EU heads of state or government meet as the European Council. Council presidency: Netherlands.

events.title: George Chambers takes power
events.summary: George Michael Chambers ORTT was a Trinidadian politician who served as the 2nd Prime Minister of Trinidad and Tobago from 1981 to 1986. He was a member of the People's National Movement and sat in the House of Representatives representing Saint Ann's East from 1956 to 1986. He held multiple ministerial positions under Prime Minister Eric Williams.

events.title: Battle: H-3 airstrike
events.summary: The H-3 airstrike was a surprise air attack by the Iranian Air Force during the Iran–Iraq War on 4 April 1981 against the Iraqi Air Force's H-3 Air Base in western Iraq. The Iranians destroyed at least 48 Iraqi aircraft on the ground with no losses of their own.

events.title: Mitenand Initiative
events.summary: The Solidarity for a new policy on foreigners popular initiative was a Swiss federal popular initiative, rejected by the voters and cantons on 5 April 1981.

events.title: Mark Eyskens takes power
events.summary: Marc Maria Frans, Viscount Eyskens, known as Mark Eyskens, is a Belgian economist, professor and politician in the Christian People's Party, now called Christian Democratic and Flemish, and briefly served as the prime minister of Belgium in 1981.

events.title: 1981 Brixton riot
events.summary: The 1981 Brixton riot, or Brixton uprising, was a series of clashes between mainly black youths and the Metropolitan Police in Brixton, London, between 10 and 12 April 1981.

events.title: Coup: Operation Red Dog
events.summary: Operation Red Dog was a failed 1981 plot to overthrow the government of Dominica and restore former prime minister Patrick John to power. Its participants included long-time Ku Klux Klan member Mike Perdue, German-Canadian Nazi Wolfgang Droege, American white nationalist Don Black, Canadian James Alexander McQuirter, and plot leader Sydney Burnett-Alleyne.

events.title: 1981 French presidential election
events.summary: Presidential elections were held in France on 26 April 1981, with a second round on 10 May. François Mitterrand defeated incumbent president, Valéry Giscard d'Estaing to become the first Socialist president of the Fifth Republic.

events.title: 1981 Liechtenstein constitutional referendum
events.summary: A constitutional referendum was held in Liechtenstein on 10 May 1981. Voters were asked whether they approved of amending article 46, which covered the number of seats in the Landtag, its membership and the electoral system. The proposal, which had been narrowly rejected in a 1975 referendum, was rejected by 52.9% of voters.

events.title: Sergej Kraigher takes power
events.summary: Sergej Kraigher was a Yugoslav communist politician from Slovenia who served as the President of the Presidency of Yugoslavia from 1981 to 1982.

events.title: François Mitterrand takes power
events.summary: François Marie Adrien Maurice Mitterrand was President of France from 1981 to 1995. He was the first left-wing politician to assume the presidency under the Fifth Republic, successfully remaining in office longer than any other republican head of state in French history.

events.title: 1981 Cypriot legislative election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Cyprus on 24 May 1981. AKEL and the Democratic Rally both won 12 of the 35 seats. Voter turnout was 95.7%.

events.title: 1981 Dutch general election
events.summary: General elections were held in the Netherlands on 26 May 1981. The Christian Democratic Appeal (CDA) emerged as the largest party, winning 48 of the 150 seats in the House of Representatives.

events.title: Assassination of Ziaur Rahman
events.summary: Ziaur Rahman, the sixth president of Bangladesh, was assassinated by members of the Bangladesh Army on 30 May 1981 in the southeastern port city of Chittagong. Rahman went to Chittagong to arbitrate in a clash between the local leaders of his political party, the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP).

events.title: Pandemic: Epidemiology of HIV/AIDS
events.summary: The global pandemic of HIV/AIDS began in 1981, and is an ongoing worldwide public health issue. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), by 2023, HIV/AIDS had killed approximately 40.4 million people, and approximately 39 million people were infected with HIV globally. Of these, 29.8 million people (75%) are receiving antiretroviral treatment.

events.title: 1981 Bulgarian parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Bulgaria on 7 June 1981. The Fatherland Front, dominated by the Bulgarian Communist Party, was the only organisation to contest the election; all candidate lists had to be approved by the Front. The Front nominated one candidate for each constituency.

events.title: 1981 Irish general election
events.summary: The 1981 Irish general election to the 22nd Dáil was held on Thursday, 11 June, following the dissolution of the 21st Dáil on 21 May by President Patrick Hillery on the request of Taoiseach Charles Haughey.

events.title: 1981 East German general election
events.summary: General elections were held in East Germany on 14 June 1981.

events.title: 1981 Barbadian general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Barbados on 18 June 1981. The result was a victory for the ruling Barbados Labour Party, which won 17 of the 27 seats. Voter turnout was 71.6%.

events.title: 1981 French legislative election
events.summary: Legislative elections were held in France on 14 and 21 June 1981, to elect the seventh National Assembly of the Fifth Republic. The elections were called after François Mitterrand won the 1981 presidential elections and subsequently dissolved the National Assembly.

events.title: Treaty signed: African Charter on Human and Peoples' Rights
events.summary: The African Charter on Human and Peoples' Rights is an international human rights instrument that is intended to promote and protect human rights and basic freedoms in the African continent.

events.title: Giovanni Spadolini takes power
events.summary: Giovanni Spadolini was an Italian politician and statesman, who served as the 44th prime minister of Italy. He had been a leading figure in the Republican Party and the first head of a government to not be a member of Christian Democrats since 1945. He was also a newspaper editor, journalist and historian.

events.title: European Council meeting
events.summary: EU heads of state or government meet as the European Council. Council presidency: Netherlands.

events.title: Garret FitzGerald takes power
events.summary: Garret Desmond FitzGerald was an Irish Fine Gael politician, economist, and barrister who served twice as Taoiseach, serving from 1981 to 1982 and 1982 to 1987. He served as Leader of Fine Gael from 1977 to 1987 and was twice Leader of the Opposition between 1977 and 1982; he was previously Minister for Foreign Affairs from 1973 to 1977.

events.title: 1981 Israeli legislative election
events.summary: Legislative elections were held in Israel on 30 June 1981 to elect the 120 members of the Knesset. The ruling Likud won one more seat than the opposition Alignment, in line with many polls which had predicted a tight race. Voter turnout was 78.5%, with Likud receiving around ten thousand more than the Alignment.

events.title: 1981 Norwegian parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Norway on 13 and 14 September 1981. The elections led to the end of the Labour Party minority government and the creation of a Conservative Party minority government.

events.title: 7th G7 summit
events.summary: The 7th G7 Summit was called the Ottawa Summit, and was held in Montebello, Quebec, Canada and nearby Ottawa between July 20 and 21, 1981. The venue for the summit meetings was the Château Montebello.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Gambia vs NRC
events.summary: UCDP records an internationalised civil conflict between Government of Gambia (backed by Government of Senegal) and NRC over control of the government, starting 1981-07-30. This episode was active in 1 year (1981–1981), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1981-08-05.

events.title: Florez Aguilar takes power (irregular seizure of power)
Armed conflict breaks out: South Africa vs ANC
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of South Africa and ANC over control of the government, starting 1981-08-07. This episode was active in 3 years (1981–1983), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1983-12-31.

events.title: Battle: Gulf of Sidra incident (1981)
events.summary: In the first Gulf of Sidra incident, 19 August 1981, two Libyan Sukhoi Su-22M3 Fitter-G fired upon two U.S. Grumman F-14A Tomcats and were subsequently shot down off the Libyan coast.

events.title: Mauno Koivisto takes power
events.summary: Mauno Henrik Koivisto was a Finnish politician who served as the president of Finland from 1982 to 1994. He also served as the country's prime minister twice, from 1968 to 1970 and again from 1979 to 1982. He was also the first member of the Social Democratic Party to be elected as President of Finland.

events.title: Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting 1981
events.summary: The 1981 Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting was the sixth Meeting of the Heads of Government of the Commonwealth of Nations. It was held in Melbourne, Victoria, between 30 September 1981 and 7 October 1981, and was hosted by Australian Prime Minister Malcolm Fraser.

events.title: Assassination of Anwar Sadat
events.summary: On 6 October 1981, Anwar Sadat, the 3rd president of Egypt, was assassinated during the annual victory parade held in Cairo to celebrate the victory over Israel in the Yom Kippur War. The assassination was undertaken by members of the Egyptian Islamic Jihad.

events.title: 1981 Egyptian presidential confirmation referendum
events.summary: Presidential elections were held in Egypt on 13 October 1981 following the assassination of President Anwar Sadat on 6 October. House of Representatives speaker Sufi Abu Taleb became acting president until the new president was elected. The vote took the form of a referendum on the candidacy of vice president and interim prime minister Hosni Mubarak.

events.title: Kåre Willoch takes power
events.summary: Kåre Isaachsen Willoch was a Norwegian politician who served as the prime minister of Norway from 1981 to 1986 and as leader of the Conservative Party from 1970 to 1974. He previously served as the minister of trade and shipping from August to September 1963 and 1965 to 1970, and as the president of the Nordic Council in 1973.

events.title: 1981 Greek parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Greece on Sunday, 18 October 1981. PASOK, led by Andreas Papandreou, faced New Democracy, led by Georgios Rallis. Papandreou achieved a landslide victory and PASOK formed the first socialist government in the history of Greece.

events.title: Wojciech Jaruzelski takes power
events.summary: Wojciech Witold Jaruzelski was a Polish military general, politician and de facto leader of the Polish People's Republic from 1981 until 1989, serving as a military dictator from 13 December 1981 until 22 July 1983.

events.title: Andreas Papandreou takes power
events.summary: Andreas Georgiou Papandreou was a Greek academic and economist who was prime minister of Greece from 1981 to 1989 and again from 1993 to 1996. He founded PASOK, the Panhellenic Socialist Movement.

events.title: Valence Congress
events.summary: The Valence Congress was the ninth national congress of the French Socialist Party. It took place from 23 to 25 October 1981, shortly after Mitterrand's 1981 election.

events.title: North–South Summit
events.summary: The North–South Summit, officially the International Meeting on Cooperation and Development, was an international summit held in Cancún, Mexico, from 22 to 23 October 1981. The summit was attended by representatives of 22 countries from five continents. It is the only north-south summit conference in history.

events.title: 1981 Belgian general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Belgium on 8 November 1981. Voter turnout was 94.5% in the Chamber election and 94.6% in the Senate election. Elections were also held for the nine provincial councils and for the Council of the German Cultural Community. They were the first elections after the voting age was lowered from 21 to 18.

events.title: 1981 Trinidad and Tobago general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Trinidad and Tobago on 9 November 1981. The result was a victory for the People's National Movement, which won 26 of the 36 seats. Voter turnout was 56.4%.

events.title: Coup: 1981 Seychelles coup attempt
events.summary: The 1981 Seychelles coup d'état attempt, sometimes referred to as the Seychelles affair or Operation Angela, was a failed South African–orchestrated coup to overthrow the government of Prime Minister France-Albert René in Seychelles and restore the previous president, James Mancham, to power.

events.title: European Council meeting
events.summary: EU heads of state or government meet as the European Council. Council presidency: United Kingdom.

events.title: 1981 Honduran general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Honduras on 29 November 1981. Each voter had a single vote to cast for a presidential candidate, with seats in the National Congress divided based on the share of the vote their presidential candidate had won. The result was a victory for Roberto Suazo Córdova of the Liberal Party, who received 54% of the vote.

events.title: 1981 Danish general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Denmark on 8 December 1981. The election was followed by a two-week crisis over the formation of a new government before the Social Democratic Party resumed its minority government.

events.title: 1981 Andorran parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Andorra on 9 December 1981, with a second round of voting on 16 December. Local elections were held on the same day. Following the elections, Òscar Ribas Reig became the country's first Prime Minister.

events.title: 1981 Maltese general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Malta on 12 December 1981.

events.title: Wilfried Martens takes power
events.summary: Wilfried Achiel Emma Martens was a Belgian politician who served as prime minister of Belgium from 1979 to 1992, except from April to December 1981. A member of the Flemish Christian People's Party, during his premiership he oversaw the transformation of Belgium into a federal state. He was one of the founders of the European People's Party.

events.title: 1981 Cuban parliamentary election
events.summary: Indirect parliamentary elections were held in Cuba on 28 December 1981.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Ghana vs Military faction (forces of Jerry John Rawlings)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Ghana and Military faction (forces of Jerry John Rawlings) over control of the government, starting 1981-12-31. This episode was active in 1 year (1981–1981), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1981-12-31.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Indonesia vs OPM (West Papua)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Indonesia and OPM over control of West Papua, starting 1981-12-31. This episode was active in 1 year (1981–1981), 1 of them at war level (1,000+ battle deaths a year), and ended 1981-12-31.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Malaysia vs CPM
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Malaysia and CPM over control of the government, starting 1981-12-31. This episode was active in 1 year (1981–1981), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1981-12-31.

events.title: Fritz Honegger takes power
events.summary: Fritz Honegger was a Swiss politician.

events.title: 1982 Finnish presidential election
events.summary: Two-stage presidential elections were held in Finland in January 1982. The public elected presidential electors to an electoral college on 17 and 18 January. They in turn elected the president.

events.title: Roberto Suazo Córdova takes power
events.summary: Roberto Suazo Córdova was the 29th President of Honduras from 27 January 1982 until 27 January 1986. Suazo Córdova died on 22 December 2018 following an ulcer surgical operation at the age of 91.

events.title: 1982 Costa Rican general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Costa Rica on 7 February 1982. Luis Alberto Monge of the National Liberation Party won the presidential election, whilst his party also won the parliamentary election. Voter turnout was 79%.

events.title: February 1982 Irish general election
events.summary: The February 1982 Irish general election to the 23rd Dáil was held on Thursday, 18 February, three weeks after the dissolution of the 22nd Dáil on 27 January by President Patrick Hillery on the request of Taoiseach Garret FitzGerald on the defeat of the government's budget.

events.title: 1982 Greenlandic European Communities membership referendum
events.summary: A referendum on continued membership of the European Communities (EC) was held in Greenland on 23 February 1982.

events.title: Dario Paredes takes power (irregular seizure of power)
1982 Guatemalan general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Guatemala on 7 March 1982. Ángel Aníbal Guevara, hand-picked successor of previous president Romeo Lucas García, was declared the winner of the presidential election and was scheduled to take office on 1 July.

events.title: Charles Haughey takes power
events.summary: Charles James Haughey was an Irish politician who served as Taoiseach three times between 1979 and 1992, when he was leader of Fianna Fáil. Over a forty-year career, Haughey was the most complex and divisive figure in late 20th-century Ireland.

events.title: Efraín Ríos Montt takes power (irregular seizure of power)
events.summary: José Efraín Ríos Montt was a Guatemalan military officer who served as de facto President of Guatemala from 1982 to 1983. His brief tenure as chief executive was one of the bloodiest periods in the long-running Guatemalan Civil War.

events.title: 1982 Salvadoran presidential election
events.summary: Presidential elections were held in El Salvador on 29 April 1982. The election was indirect rather than being a popular vote; the Constitutional Assembly voted on three candidates nominated by the Armed Forces of El Salvador (FAES). Álvaro Magaña, a moderate and the leader of the Democratic Action Party (AD), won the election with 36 votes.

events.title: 1982 Salvadoran Constitutional Assembly election
events.summary: Constitutional Assembly elections were held in El Salvador on 28 March 1982. The Christian Democratic Party won a plurality, with 24 of the 60 seats. Voter turnout was 68.0%. A coalition government, representing the three largest parties equally, was subsequently formed under the presidency of Álvaro Magaña.

events.title: European Council meeting
events.summary: EU heads of state or government meet as the European Council. Council presidency: Belgium.

events.title: Argentina invades the Falkland Islands
events.summary: The Falklands War was a ten-week war in the South Atlantic in 1982 between Argentina and the United Kingdom over possession of the Falkland Islands and its dependencies of South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands. The conflict began on 2 April 1982 when Argentina invaded the Falkland Islands, followed by the invasion of South Georgia the next day.

events.title: 1982 Northwest Territories division plebiscite
events.summary: The Northwest Territories division plebiscite was a stand-alone, territory-wide plebiscite conducted on April 14, 1982. This was the first territory-wide plebiscite conducted in Northwest Territories history.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Nicaragua vs Contras
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Nicaragua and Contras over control of the government, starting 1982-04-17. This episode was active in 9 years (1982–1990), 6 of them at war level (1,000+ battle deaths a year), and ended 1990-04-15.

events.title: Battle of Khorramshahr (1982)
events.summary: The Second Battle of Khorramshahr, also known in Iran as the Liberation of Khorramshahr was the Iranian recapture of the city of Khorramshahr on 24 May 1982, during the Iran–Iraq War. The city had been captured by the Iraqis earlier in the war, on 26 October 1980, shortly after the Iraqi invasion of Iran.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Venezuela vs Bandera Roja
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Venezuela and Bandera Roja over control of the government, starting 1982-04-30. This episode was active in 1 year (1982–1982), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1982-10-04.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Argentina – United Kingdom (Malvinas/Falkland Islands)
events.summary: UCDP records an interstate conflict between Government of Argentina and Government of United Kingdom over control of Malvinas/Falkland Islands, starting 1982-05-02. This episode was active in 1 year (1982–1982), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1982-06-14.

events.title: 1982 Saint Lucian general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Saint Lucia on 3 May 1982. The result was a victory for the United Workers Party, which won fourteen of the seventeen seats. Voter turnout was 65.8%.

events.title: Assassination of Orhan Gündüz
events.summary: The assassination of Orhan Gündüz, Turkish businessman and diplomat, took place on May 4, 1982, in Somerville, Massachusetts, United States.

events.title: 1982 Dominican Republic general election
events.summary: General elections were held in the Dominican Republic on 16 May 1982. Salvador Jorge Blanco of the Dominican Revolutionary Party won the presidential election, whilst his party also won the parliamentary elections. Voter turnout was 73% in the presidential election and 72% in the parliamentary election.

events.title: Petar Stambolić takes power
events.summary: Petar Stambolić was a Serbian communist politician who served as the President of the Federal Executive Council of Yugoslavia from 1963 to 1967 and as President of the Presidency from 1982 until 1983.

events.title: 1982 Andorran electoral system referendum
events.summary: A referendum on the electoral system was held in Andorra on 28 May 1982.

events.title: Battle of Goose Green
events.summary: The Battle of Goose Green was fought from the 28th to the 29th of May 1982 by British and Argentine forces during the Falklands War. Located on East Falkland's central isthmus, the settlement of Goose Green was the site of a tactically vital airfield.

events.title: 1982 visit by Pope John Paul II to the United Kingdom
events.summary: The visit of Pope John Paul II to the United Kingdom in 1982 was the first visit there by a reigning pope. The Pope arrived in the UK on Friday 28 May, and during his time there visited nine cities, delivering 16 major addresses.

events.title: 8th G7 summit
events.summary: The 8th G7 Summit was held at the Palace of Versailles, France, from 4 to 6 June 1982.

events.title: Assassination of Erkut Akbay
events.summary: The assassination of Erkut Akbay refers to the murder of the Turkish administrative attache, Erkut Akbay, 40, in Lisbon, where the diplomat was serving, on 7 June 1982. Akbay was assassinated near his home on the outskirts of the city as he returned home for lunch with his wife.

events.title: 1982 Bahamian general election
events.summary: General elections were held in the Bahamas on 10 June 1982. The result was a victory for the Progressive Liberal Party, which won 32 of the 43 seats. Janet Bostwick of the Free National Movement (FNM) became the first female member of the House of Assembly.

events.title: 1982 Bonn NATO summit
events.summary: The 1982 Bonn summit was the 6th NATO summit bringing the leaders of member nations together at the same time. The formal sessions and informal meetings in Bonn took place on 10 June 1982. This event was only the seventh meeting of the NATO heads of state following the ceremonial signing of the North Atlantic Treaty on 4 April 1949.

events.title: Fahd of Saudi Arabia of Saudi Arabia takes power
events.summary: Fahd bin Abdulaziz Al Saud was King and Prime Minister of Saudi Arabia from 13 June 1982 until his death in 2005. Prior to his ascension, he was Crown Prince of Saudi Arabia from 1975 to 1982.

events.title: European Council meeting
events.summary: EU heads of state or government meet as the European Council. Council presidency: Belgium.

events.title: Jacobo Majluta Azar takes power
events.summary: Jacobo Majluta Azar was 47th president of the Dominican Republic for a month in 1982. He was previously the 32nd vice president under President Antonio Guzmán Fernández from 1978 until his accession to the presidency. Following Fernández's death in July 1982, Majluta completed his term and handed over power to Salvador Jorge Blanco the following month.

events.title: 1982 Mexican general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Mexico on 4 July 1982. The presidential elections were won by Miguel de la Madrid, who received 74% of the vote. In the Chamber of Deputies election, the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) won 299 of the 372 seats, as well as winning 63 of the 64 seats in the Senate election.

events.title: Terrorist attack: Hyde Park and Regent's Park bombings
events.summary: The Hyde Park and Regent's Park bombings were carried out on 20 July 1982 in London, England. Members of the Provisional Irish Republican Army (IRA) detonated two improvised explosive devices during British military ceremonies in Hyde Park and Regent's Park, both in central London.

events.title: 1982 San Marino citizenship referendum
events.summary: A referendum on the citizenship law was held in San Marino on 25 July 1982. The proposed abolition of the law failed, with 57.3% voting against it.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: India vs PLA (Manipur)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of India and PLA over control of Manipur, starting 1982-07-31. This episode was active in 7 years (1982–1988), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1988-12-31.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Iraq vs SCIRI
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Iraq and SCIRI over control of the government, starting 1982-08-01. This episode was active in 3 years (1982–1984), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1984-12-31.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Kenya vs Military faction (forces of Hezekiah Ochuka)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Kenya and Military faction (forces of Hezekiah Ochuka) over control of the government, starting 1982-08-01. This episode was active in 1 year (1982–1982), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1982-08-21.

events.title: Battle: Operation Ramadan
events.summary: Operation Ramadan was an Iranian offensive in the Iran–Iraq War that consisted of three separate attacks that lasted for 6 weeks. It was launched by Iran on 13 July 1982 near Basra and featured the use of human wave attacks in the largest land battle since World War II. The engagement was a part of the overall stalemate.

events.title: 1982 Equatorial Guinean constitutional referendum
events.summary: A constitutional referendum was held in Equatorial Guinea on 15 August 1982 following the overthrow and execution of Francisco Macías Nguema in the 1979 coup d'état.

events.title: Salvador Jorge Blanco takes power
events.summary: José Salvador Omar Jorge Blanco was a Dominican politician, lawyer and writer who served as the 48th president of the Dominican Republic from 1982 to 1986. He was a Senator running for the PRD party. He started his political career as a Committee Secretary for the Unión Cívica de Santiago in 1963 and joined the PRD in 1964.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Peru vs Sendero Luminoso
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Peru and Sendero Luminoso over control of the government, starting 1982-08-22. This episode was active in 18 years (1982–1999), 8 of them at war level (1,000+ battle deaths a year), and ended 1999-11-26.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Lebanon vs NSF
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Lebanon and NSF over control of the government, starting 1982-09-01. This episode was active in 5 years (1982–1986), 1 of them at war level (1,000+ battle deaths a year), and ended 1986-12-31.

events.title: 1982 Dutch general election
events.summary: Early general elections were held in the Netherlands on 8 September 1982. The Labour Party emerged as the largest party, winning 47 of the 150 seats in the House of Representatives; however, this would be the last time it did so until 1994.

events.title: Poul Schlüter takes power
events.summary: Poul Holmskov Schlüter was a Danish politician who served as Prime Minister of Denmark from 1982 to 1993. He was the first member of the Conservative People's Party to become prime minister, as well as the first conservative to hold the office since 1901. Schlüter was a member of the Folketing for the Conservative People's Party from 1964 to 1994.

events.title: Assassination of Bachir Gemayel
events.summary: On 14 September 1982, a bomb was detonated during a meeting of the right-wing Kataeb Party in the Beirut neighbourhood of Achrafieh. Militia commander and Lebanese president-elect Bashir Gemayel and 23 other Kataeb Party politicians were killed in the attack.

events.title: 1982 Swedish general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Sweden on 19 September 1982. They saw the return of the Swedish Social Democratic Party to power after six years in opposition, the longest period in opposition by the Social Democrats since the 1910s.

events.title: Helmut Kohl takes power
events.summary: Helmut Josef Michael Kohl was a German politician who served as chancellor of Germany from 1982 to 1998. He was leader of the Christian Democratic Union (CDU) from 1973 to 1998 and oversaw the end of the Cold War, German reunification, and the creation of the European Union (EU).

events.title: Olof Palme takes power
events.summary: Sven Olof Joachim Palme was a Swedish politician and statesman who served as Prime Minister of Sweden from 1969 to 1976 and 1982 to 1986. Palme led the Swedish Social Democratic Party from 1969 until his assassination in 1986.

events.title: Coup: 1982 Spanish coup attempt
events.summary: The 1982 coup d'état attempt was a Spanish conspiracy conceived by members of the military to overthrow the government that was meant to take place on 27 October 1982, the day before national elections. The plan was discovered and the planners were arrested on 2 October.

events.title: 1982 Spanish general election
events.summary: A general election was held in Spain on 28 October 1982 to elect the members of the 2nd Cortes Generales under the Spanish Constitution of 1978. All 350 seats in the Congress of Deputies were up for election, as well as 208 of 254 seats in the Senate.

events.title: Ruud Lubbers takes power
events.summary: Rudolphus Franciscus Marie "Ruud" Lubbers was a Dutch politician, diplomat and businessman who served as prime minister of the Netherlands from 1982 to 1994, and as United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees from 2001 to 2005. He was a member of the Catholic People's Party (KVP), which later merged to become the Christian Democratic Appeal (CDA) party.

events.title: 1982 Turkish constitutional referendum
events.summary: A constitutional referendum was held in Turkey on 7 November 1982. Voters approved the new constitution and the presidency of Kenan Evren with a 91.37% "yes" vote, with a 91% turnout.

events.title: Yuri Andropov takes power
events.summary: Yuri Vladimirovich Andropov was a Soviet politician who served as the general secretary of the Communist Party of the Soviet Union from late 1982 until his death in 1984. He previously served as the chairman of the KGB from 1967 until 1982.

events.title: 1982 Albanian parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in the People's Socialist Republic of Albania on 14 November 1982. The Democratic Front was the only party able to contest the elections, and subsequently won all 250 seats. Voter turnout was reported to be 100%.

events.title: November 1982 Irish general election
events.summary: The November 1982 Irish general election to the 24th Dáil was held on Wednesday, 24 November, three weeks after the dissolution of the 23rd Dáil on 4 November by President Patrick Hillery, on the request of Taoiseach Charles Haughey following a defeat of the government in a motion of confidence.

events.title: Yasuhiro Nakasone takes power
events.summary: Yasuhiro Nakasone was a Japanese politician who served as Prime Minister of Japan from 1982 to 1987. His political term was best known for pushing through the privatization of state-owned companies, pursuing a hawkish and pro-United States foreign policy and his rejection of Keynesianism and his support of neoliberalism.

events.title: Amintore Fanfani takes power
events.summary: Amintore Fanfani was an Italian politician and statesman who served as 32nd prime minister of Italy for five separate terms. He was one of the best-known Italian politicians after the Second World War and a historical figure of the left-wing faction of Christian Democracy. He is also considered one of the founders of the modern Italian centre-left.

events.title: Miguel de la Madrid takes power
events.summary: Miguel de la Madrid Hurtado was a Mexican politician and lawyer affiliated with the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) who served as the 59th president of Mexico from 1982 to 1988.

events.title: European Council meeting
events.summary: EU heads of state or government meet as the European Council. Council presidency: Denmark.

events.title: Assassination: December murders
events.summary: The December murders were the murders on 7, 8, and 9 December 1982, of fifteen prominent young Surinamese men who had criticized the military dictatorship then ruling Suriname. Thirteen of these men were arrested on December 7 between 2 am and 5 am while sleeping in their homes.

events.title: Treaty signed: United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea
events.summary: The United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), also called the Law of the Sea Convention or the Law of the Sea Treaty, is an international treaty that establishes a legal framework for all marine and maritime activities. As of October 2024, 169 sovereign states and the European Union are parties to the convention.

events.title: Garret FitzGerald takes power
events.summary: Garret Desmond FitzGerald was an Irish Fine Gael politician, economist, and barrister who served twice as Taoiseach, serving from 1981 to 1982 and 1982 to 1987. He served as Leader of Fine Gael from 1977 to 1987 and was twice Leader of the Opposition between 1977 and 1982; he was previously Minister for Foreign Affairs from 1973 to 1977.

events.title: 1982 Sri Lankan parliamentary term extension referendum
events.summary: A referendum on extending the term of parliament by six years was held in Sri Lanka on 22 December 1982. It was the first and so far only national referendum to be held in the country. The referendum was called for by President J. R. Jayawardene, who had been elected to a fresh six-year term as President in October 1982.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Somalia vs SSDF
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Somalia and SSDF over control of the government, starting 1982-12-31. This episode was active in 3 years (1982–1984), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1984-12-31.

events.title: Pierre Aubert takes power
events.summary: Pierre Aubert was a Swiss politician, lawyer and member of the Swiss Federal Council (1978–1987) from the canton of Neuchâtel. He was a member of the Social Democratic Party (SP/PS).

events.title: 1983 Monegasque general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Monaco on 9 January 1983. The result was a victory for the National and Democratic Union, which won all 18 seats in the National Council.

events.title: 1983 Cypriot presidential election
events.summary: Presidential elections were held in Cyprus on 13 February 1983. The result was a victory for Spyros Kyprianou of the Democratic Party, who received 56.5% of the vote. Voter turnout was 95.0%.

events.title: Nellie massacre
events.summary: The Nellie massacre took place in central Assam during a seven-hour period on the morning of 18 February 1983. The massacre claimed the lives of 2000–3000 people from 14 villages—Alisingha, Khulapathar, Basundhari, Bugduba Beel, Bugduba Habi, Borjola, Butuni, Dongabori, Indurmari, Mati Parbat, Muladhari, Mati Parbat no.

events.title: 1983 West German federal election
events.summary: A federal election was held in West Germany on 6 March 1983 to elect the members of the 10th Bundestag. The CDU/CSU alliance led by Helmut Kohl remained the largest faction in parliament, with Kohl remaining Chancellor.

events.title: Assassination of Galip Balkar
events.summary: Galip Balkar, Turkish ambassador to Yugoslavia, was shot on 9 March 1983 in downtown Belgrade, capital of Yugoslavia. He died two days later as a consequence. The responsibility for the attack was taken by the Justice Commandos of the Armenian Genocide (JCAG), an Armenian militant group.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Ethiopia vs SLM (Sidamaland)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Ethiopia and SLM over control of Sidamaland, starting 1983-03-16. This episode was active in 1 year (1983–1983), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1983-12-31.

events.title: European Council meeting
events.summary: EU heads of state or government meet as the European Council. Council presidency: West Germany.

events.title: 1983 Finnish parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Finland on 20 and 21 March 1983. The elections were widely regarded as a "protest election" because, contrary to expectations, the major parties with the exception of the Social Democratic Party (SDP) performed poorly; the Liberal People's Party (LKP) lost all its seats in the Eduskunta, while the Finnish Rural Party…

events.title: 1983 Israeli presidential election
events.summary: An election for President of Israel was held in the Knesset on 22 March 1983 in which Chaim Herzog was elected the sixth president of the state of Israel.

events.title: Terrorist attack: 1983 US embassy bombing in Beirut
events.summary: The April 18, 1983, United States Embassy bombing was a suicide bombing on the Embassy of the United States in Beirut, Lebanon, that killed 32 Lebanese, 17 Americans, and 14 visitors and passers-by. The victims were mostly embassy and CIA staff members, but also included several US soldiers and one U.S. Marine Security Guard.

events.title: 1983 Icelandic parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Iceland on 23 April 1983. The Independence Party remained the largest party in the Lower House of the Althing, winning 15 of the 40 seats.

events.title: 1983 Austrian legislative election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Austria on 24 April 1983. The result saw the Socialist Party win 90 of 183 seats, enough to secure them a fifth term in government, albeit without the absolute majority the party had held since 1971. This prompted Bruno Kreisky to stand down as SPÖ leader and Chancellor in favour of Fred Sinowatz.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Chad – Nigeria (Lake Chad)
events.summary: UCDP records an interstate conflict between Government of Chad and Government of Nigeria over control of Lake Chad, starting 1983-04-24. This episode was active in 1 year (1983–1983), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1983-11-01.

events.title: 1983 Panamanian constitutional referendum
events.summary: A constitutional referendum was held in Panama on 24 April 1983. Voters were asked whether they approved of a series of amendments to the 1972 constitution. A reported 87.8% voted in favour, with a turnout of 66.8%.

events.title: 1983 Portuguese legislative election
events.summary: The 1983 Portuguese legislative election took place on 25 April. The election renewed all 250 members of the Assembly of the Republic.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Sudan vs SPLM/A
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Sudan and SPLM/A over control of the government, starting 1983-05-17. This episode was active in 36 years (1983–2018), 26 of them at war level (1,000+ battle deaths a year), and ended 2018-12-16.

events.title: Fred Sinowatz takes power
events.summary: Alfred Sinowatz was an Austrian historian and politician of the Social Democratic Party (SPÖ), who served as Chancellor of Austria from 1983 to 1986. Prior to becoming Chancellor, he had served as Minister of Education from 1971 to 1983 and Vice-Chancellor from 1981 to 1983.

events.title: Steingrímur Hermannsson takes power
events.summary: Steingrímur Hermannsson was an Icelandic politician who served as prime minister of Iceland from 1983 to 1987, and again from 1988 to 1991. He was the chairman for the Progressive Party from 1979 to 1994.

events.title: 9th G7 summit
events.summary: The 9th G7 Summit was held at Williamsburg, Virginia, United States between May 28 and 30, 1983. The venue for the summit meetings was Colonial Williamsburg in Virginia.

events.title: 1983 San Marino general election
events.summary: General elections were held in San Marino on 29 May 1983. The Sammarinese Christian Democratic Party remained the largest party, winning 26 of the 60 seats in the Grand and General Council. Following the elections the Sammarinese Communist Party continued their coalition with the Sammarinese Socialist Party and the Unitary Socialist Party.

events.title: 1983 United Kingdom general election
events.summary: A general election was held in the United Kingdom on Thursday 9 June 1983. The governing Conservative Party, under the leadership of Margaret Thatcher, won a landslide victory with a majority of 144 seats.

events.title: European Council meeting
events.summary: EU heads of state or government meet as the European Council. Council presidency: West Germany.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Ghana vs Military faction (forces of Ekow Dennis and Edward Adjei-Ampofo)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Ghana and Military faction (forces of Ekow Dennis and Edward Adjei-Ampofo)  over control of the government, starting 1983-06-19. This episode was active in 1 year (1983–1983), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1983-06-19.

events.title: 1983 Italian general election
events.summary: The 1983 Italian general election was held in Italy on 26 June 1983. The Pentapartito formula, the governative alliance between five centrist parties, caused unexpected problems to Christian Democracy. The alliance was fixed and universal, extended both to the national government and to the local administrations.

events.title: Black July
events.summary: Black July was an anti-Tamil pogrom that occurred in Sri Lanka during July 1983. The pogrom was premeditated, and was finally triggered by a deadly ambush on a Sri Lankan Army patrol by the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) on 23 July 1983, which killed 13 soldiers.

events.title: Terrorist attack: 1983 Turkish embassy attack in Lisbon
events.summary: The 1983 Turkish embassy attack was an attack on the Turkish embassy in Lisbon on 27 July 1983, which resulted in the death of 7 people, including all 5 attackers.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Ethiopia vs OLF (Oromiya)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of Ethiopia and OLF over control of Oromiya, starting 1983-07-31. This episode was active in 10 years (1983–1992), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1992-06-30.

events.title: Bettino Craxi takes power
events.summary: Benedetto "Bettino" Craxi was an Italian politician and statesman, leader of the Italian Socialist Party (PSI) from 1976 to 1993, and the 45th prime minister of Italy from 1983 to 1987. He was the first PSI member to become prime minister and the second from a socialist party to hold the office.

events.title: Coup: 1983 Upper Voltan coup d'état
events.summary: On 4 August 1983, a coup d'état was launched in the Republic of Upper Volta in an event sometimes referred to as the August revolution or Burkinabé revolution. It was carried out by radical elements of the army led by Thomas Sankara and Blaise Compaoré, against the regime of Major Jean-Baptiste Ouédraogo.

events.title: Óscar Humberto Mejía Víctores takes power (irregular seizure of power)
events.summary: Óscar Humberto Mejía Víctores was a Guatemalan military officer and politician who served as the Head of Government from August 1983 to January 1986. A member of the military, he was head of state during the apex of repression and death squad activity in the Central American nation.

events.title: Manuel Noriega takes power (irregular seizure of power)
events.summary: Manuel Antonio Noriega Moreno was a Panamanian military officer and dictator who was the de facto ruler of Panama from 1983 to 1989. He never officially served as president of Panama, instead ruling as an unelected military dictator through puppet presidents.

events.title: Assassination of Ninoy Aquino
events.summary: On August 21, 1983, on the apron of what was then Manila International Airport, Benigno "Ninoy" Aquino Jr., a former Philippine senator, was assassinated with a gunshot to the head.

events.title: Eighth Amendment of the Constitution of Ireland
events.summary: The Eighth Amendment of the Constitution Act 1983 was an amendment to the Constitution of Ireland which inserted a subsection recognising "the equal right to life of the pregnant woman and the unborn".

events.title: Terrorist attack: Gulf Air Flight 771
events.summary: Gulf Air Flight 771 was an international scheduled passenger flight from Jinnah International Airport, Karachi, Pakistan, to Abu Dhabi International Airport, Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates.

events.title: 1983 Labour Party leadership election (UK)
events.summary: The 1983 Labour Party leadership election was an election in the United Kingdom for the leadership of the Labour Party. It occurred when Michael Foot resigned as Leader after the party won only 209 seats at the 1983 general election, a loss of 60 seats from its performance at the previous election four years earlier.

events.title: Terrorist attack: Rangoon bombing
events.summary: The Rangoon bombing of 9 October 1983 was an assassination attempt orchestrated by North Korea against Chun Doo-hwan, the fifth president of South Korea, in Rangoon, Burma. Although Chun survived, 21 people died in the attack and 46 were injured.

events.title: Yitzhak Shamir takes power
events.summary: Yitzhak Shamir was an Israeli politician who served as the seventh prime minister of Israel, serving two terms. Before the establishment of the State of Israel, Shamir was a leader of the Zionist militant group Lehi, also known as the Stern Gang.

events.title: Terrorist attack: 1983 Beirut barracks bombings
events.summary: On October 23, 1983, two truck bombs were detonated at buildings in Beirut, Lebanon, housing American and French service members of the Multinational Force in Lebanon (MNF), a military peacekeeping operation during the Lebanese Civil War. The attack killed 307 people: 241 U.S. and 58 French military personnel, six civilians and both the attackers.

events.title: 1983 Swiss federal election
events.summary: Federal elections were held in Switzerland on 23 October 1983. The Free Democratic Party emerged as the largest party in the National Council, winning 54 of the 200 seats. It was the first time the Social Democratic Party had not received the most votes in a federal election since 1925.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: Grenada – United States of America
events.summary: UCDP records an interstate conflict between Government of Grenada and Government of United States of America over control of the government, starting 1983-10-25. This episode was active in 1 year (1983–1983), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1983-10-27.

events.title: 1983 Turkish general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Turkey on 6 November 1983, the first since 1977 after democratic rights were abandoned after the military coup of 1980. The National Security Council banned the previous political parties from participating, leading to the establishment of new parties.

events.title: 1983 South African constitutional referendum
events.summary: A referendum on a new constitution was held in South Africa on 2 November 1983 in which the white population was given the opportunity to approve or reject the Constitution of 1983.

events.title: Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting 1983
events.summary: The 1983 Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting was the seventh Meeting of the Heads of Government of the Commonwealth of Nations. It was held in New Delhi, India, between 23 and 29 November 1983, and was hosted by Indian Prime Minister Indira Gandhi. The retreat was held in Goa.

events.title: 1983 Irish presidential election
events.summary: In the 1983 Irish presidential election outgoing President Patrick Hillery agreed under enormous political pressure to seek a second term.

events.title: European Council meeting
events.summary: EU heads of state or government meet as the European Council. Council presidency: Greece.

events.title: Turgut Özal takes power
events.summary: Halil Turgut Özal was a Turkish politician, bureaucrat, engineer and statesman who served as the president of Turkey from 1989 to 1993. He previously served as the prime minister of Turkey from 1983 to 1989 as the leader of the Motherland Party. He was the deputy prime minister of Turkey in the military government of Bülend Ulusu between 1980 and 1982.

events.title: 1983 Jamaican general election
events.summary: Early general elections were held in Jamaica on 15 December 1983. The elections were effectively ended as a contest when the main opposition party, the People's National Party, boycotted the election to protest the refusal of the ruling Jamaican Labour Party to update the electoral roll amid allegations of voter fraud.

events.title: Tunisian bread riots
events.summary: The Tunisian bread riots were a series of violent demonstrations in Tunisia that occurred from December 1983 to January 1984, triggered by a rise in the price of bread due to an IMF-imposed austerity program. President Habib Bourguiba declared a state of emergency and the riots were put down by force. Over 100 rioters died.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: China – Vietnam (Various)
events.summary: UCDP records an interstate conflict between Government of China and Government of Vietnam (North Vietnam) over control of Various, starting 1983-12-31. This episode was active in 2 years (1983–1984), below war level (25–999 battle deaths a year), and ended 1984-12-31.

events.title: Armed conflict breaks out: India vs Sikh insurgents (Punjab/Khalistan)
events.summary: UCDP records a civil conflict between Government of India and Sikh insurgents over control of Punjab/Khalistan, starting 1983-12-31. This episode was active in 11 years (1983–1993), 4 of them at war level (1,000+ battle deaths a year), and ended 1993-12-24.

events.title: Leon Schlumpf takes power
events.summary: Leon Schlumpf was a Swiss politician and a member of the Swiss Federal Council (1979–1987).

events.title: 1984 Danish general election
events.summary: General elections were held in Denmark on 10 January 1984, after the opposition voted against the centre-right four-party government's state budget bill. Although the Social Democratic Party remained the largest in the Folketing with 56 of the 179 seats, the Conservative People's Party achieved its best-ever result, gaining 16 seats.

events.title: Sony Corp. of America v. Universal City Studios, Inc.
events.summary: Sony Corp. of America v. Universal City Studios, Inc., 464 U.S. 417 (1984), also known as the "Betamax case", is a decision by the Supreme Court of the United States which ruled that the making of individual copies of complete television shows for purposes of time shifting does not constitute copyright infringement, but can instead be defended as fair use.

events.title: 1984 Republican Party presidential primaries
events.summary: From February 20 to July 1, 1984, voters of the Republican Party chose its nominee for president in the 1984 United States presidential election.

events.title: 1984 Haitian parliamentary election
events.summary: Parliamentary elections were held in Haiti on 12 February 1984. All but one of the candidates were members of the National Unity Party (PUN) of President Jean-Claude Duvalier. The PUN subsequently won all 59 seats.

events.title: Konstantin Chernenko takes power
events.summary: Konstantin Ustinovich Chernenko was a Soviet politician who served as the de jure leader of the Soviet Union from February 1984 until his death in March 1985.

events.title: 1984 Soviet Union legislative election
events.summary: Supreme Soviet elections were held in the Soviet Union on 4 March 1984. The elections were called on December 16, 1983. The elections were not free and fair, as there was no genuine competition and no meaningful choice for voters to make.

events.title: 1984–1985 United Kingdom miners' strike
events.summary: From 1984 until 1985, a major miners' strike shook the British coal industry in response to proposed closures of uneconomic pits. It was led by Arthur Scargill of the National Union of Mineworkers (NUM) against the National Coal Board (NCB), a government agency.

events.title: Treaty signed: Nkomati Accord
events.summary: The Nkomati Accord was a non-aggression pact signed on 16 March 1984 between the People's Republic of Mozambique and the Republic of South Africa.
